is_missing_dep_time is derived as a boolean over dep_time, whose null_count 4883 of 166158 rows marks flights with no actual departure, so consumers can filter them deliberately instead of inferring intent from nulls.

tailnum has null_count 1521 (null_rate 0.009154) across 3825 distinct registrations; the gap is retained so aircraft-level joins can detect unmatched rows.

purpose: silver_nyc_flights is the cleaned, typed row-per-flight table built from bronze.nyc_flights (166158 rows, duplicate_row_rate 0.0), covering departures from EWR, JFK and LGA in 2013 for months 1 through 6. It carries the calendar keys, scheduled and actual clock times, delay and air-time metrics, carrier, flight number, aircraft tail number and route, and feeds downstream on-time-performance and route-volume marts.
usage: Read one row as one scheduled flight leg, identified by carrier, flight, origin and time_hour; time_hour is an hourly TIMESTAMP, while dep_time, sched_dep_time, arr_time and sched_arr_time remain integer HHMM clock values (min 1.0, max 2400.0 in bronze) and must be parsed before arithmetic. Delay and air-time columns are nullable by design; filter on is_missing_dep_time when an analysis must exclude the 4883 rows with no actual departure, and expect arr_delay and air_time to be null on 5480 rows.
limitations: The extract covers only 2013 months 1 through 6 (year distinct_count 1, month distinct_values 1.0 to 6.0), so it is not a full-year dataset. Cleanup does not reconcile the clock-time encoding: dep_time and arr_time reach 2400.0 and wrap past midnight, and no date-time column is constructed from them. Nulls are retained rather than resolved for dep_time and dep_delay (2.9388%), arr_time (3.07%), arr_delay and air_time (3.2981%) and tailnum (0.9154%), and the declared grain is unverified because the profile reports only per-column distinct counts.
